prompt: A seven-panel photo strip of the same dairy milking shed, panels side by side left to right. Each panel is numbered 1 to 7 in its top-left corner and has a day slate hung by the door naming what was delivered at that moment. In panel order the 7 day slates read: CHURN, FEED, FEED, CHURN, NOTHING, CHURN, NOTHING. Now the rule about the red warning bell. A CHURN delivery makes it ringing exactly THREE panels later than the panel it arrived in. A FEED delivery makes it ringing exactly ONE panel later than the panel it arrived in. Nothing makes it ringing in the panel where the delivery itself arrives, and a delivery whose effect would fall past the last panel simply never shows. If two deliveries happen to fall due in the same panel it is simply ringing in that panel — not twice and not more strongly. In every other panel the red warning bell is silent. I am deliberately not listing the answer anywhere in this request; work it out from the figures printed in the picture.
easy_question: This image was supposed to show a strip of separate numbered panels in a row, each panel showing the same doorway with a single word written on a card or slate beside it. Ignoring artistic quality, and ignoring whether the details are right or wrong, does the image DEPICT that? Answer NO only if the picture is unrelated to that description or contains no such arrangement at all. Answer yes or no only.
